newsitem.title: USA: US CREDIT OUTLOOK -- Retail sales, Producer prices.
newsitem.headline: US CREDIT OUTLOOK -- Retail sales, Producer prices.

text.p: The coming week will offer a fairly rich bounty of fresh economic information to the U.S. government securities market.

In contrast to the week just ended, when scant new data became available, the government in the coming week will release reports on April retail sales, wholesale prices, consumer prices, industrial production and housing starts.
Those reports measure all the key aspects of the economy -- consumer demand, manufacturing and inflation trends, analysts said.
From monthly store sales reports and from auto industry figures, economists have gathered that retail sales were weak in April.

Economists polled by Reuters estimate retail sales fell 0.3 percent last month, after a 0.2 percent increase in March. Without auto transactions, sales are forecast to have risen 0.1 percent in April, the economists said, after a 0.5 percent March increase.
The retail sales report, due on Tuesday at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT, is the first of the major economic reports of the week.

The April Producer Price Index (PPI), due on Wednesday, is expected to be unchanged after slipping 0.1 percent in March. Without its more volatile food and energy components, the core PPI is expected to be up 0.1 percent, after jumping 0.4 percent in March.

The market is very interested in the PPI report but its reaction to the wholesale price report is sometimes muted by the knowledge that the broader Consumer Price Index (CPI) report is just around the corner, analysts said.
In the coming week, the April CPI will be released on Thursday, just a day after the PPI.

The April CPI is expected to be up 0.1 percent, after edging up just 0.1 percent in March. Without its more volatile food and energy items, the CPI is likely to be up 0.2 percent after rising 0.2 percent in March.

The Federal Reserve industrial production and capacity utilization figures, due at 0915 EDT/1315 GMT on Thursday, could be affected by auto industry work stoppages that took place in April, economists said.

"A lot of people's estimates of industrial production come from the employment report (released at the beginning of the month) and these strikes spread during April," said James Glassman, senior economist at Chase Securities. "The Fed tries to get a handle on what happened over the entire month, not just during the week when they took the employment survey."

"There's no question that (the auto industry work stoppages) will show up in weaker industrial production and weaker industrial activity generally," said Josh Feinman, vice president and global markets economist at Bankers Trust.
April housing starts, due on Friday, are forecast to have occurred at an annualized rate of 1.43 million in April, compared with a 1.425 million annualized rate in March.

Besides those five reports of primary interest, the market will also get the Atlanta Fed Index and the Richmond Fed index on Tuesday and the March business inventory data on Wednesday. The government will report April real earnings data on Thursday when the Philadelphia Fed survey is also scheduled for release.
